name: Lavender
description: A silver-green shrub with purple flower spikes that smell calm, sweet and a little bit like soap.

image.alt: A field of lavender in bloom, with purple rows reaching the horizon

uses.title: Wardrobe
uses.text: Dried flowers in small cloth sachets.

uses.title: Kitchen
uses.text: A pinch in shortbread, honey or tea (use culinary lavender).

uses.title: Oil
uses.text: Essential oil is used in soaps and candles. It is for the skin and the air, not for eating.

growingTips.title: Sun
growingTips.text: Give it at least six hours of full sun a day.

growingTips.title: Soil
growingTips.text: Light, sandy and well drained. Wet soil rots the roots.

growingTips.title: Water
growingTips.text: Little and rarely, once the plant is established.

growingTips.title: Pruning
growingTips.text: Trim lightly after flowering, but never cut into the old brown wood, because it will not regrow from there.

parts.name: Flowers
parts.text: Many tiny purple flowers sit together on each spike. They bloom from June to August, and their scent comes from oil in tiny glands.

parts.name: Stems
parts.text: Like other plants in the mint family, lavender has square stems. Near the bottom they turn brown and woody over the years.

parts.name: Leaves
parts.text: The narrow leaves look silver-green because they are covered in fine hairs. The hairs help the plant keep water in hot, dry weather.

parts.name: Roots
parts.text: The roots need soil that drains fast. If they stay wet for long, they rot, which is the most common reason lavender dies.

parts.name: Bee
parts.text: Lavender is full of nectar, so bees and butterflies visit it all summer. Avoid spraying the flowers so they stay safe.
